newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower, but well up for week.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower, but well up for week.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended lower Friday, correcting after seeing good gains Thursday, but ended higher for the week.

"We saw some profit taking on light volume today, as the market appeared to have already anticipated the large LME stocks draw in yesterday's rally," Prudential Securities analyst Bette Raptopoulos said.

"Next week could be a little slow to start with also as the U.S. Columbus Day holiday Monday will slow activity and many copper traders will be still returning from the annual LME week conference in London," she said.
COMEX December copper ended down 0.75 cent at 91.50 cents a lb, after trading in a 92.90-90.90 cent range.

The COMEX December/March spread was little changed around 1.20 cents, reflecting the fall in copper warehouse stocks and prompt market tightness, after the backwardation widened from 0.50 cent in late September.
LME copper stocks fell 18,450 tonnes to 202,500 tonnes Friday, with COMEX copper stocks down 935 short tons Thursday to 17,307 short tons.
"Market participants appear to be gradually shifting their attention to copper's tight supply/demand balance," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.
"But chart based trading strategies still hold sway, with profit taking expected to kick in when prices approach the 96-97 cent resistance.
COMEX December copper last saw levels around 96 cents in early September.
Low fabricator inventories, limited scrap availability and prospects for seasonal demand strength have underpinned copper prices in recent weeks, leading to a five week closing high Thursday.
